﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AD — third Hilbert squareclass and six-bucket coprime selector packet


STATUS: POST_229AC_SELECTOR_PACKET_REFINEMENT / PROVED_EXPLICIT_BASE_HILBERT_CLASS_DELTA0 / PROVED_THREE_HILBERT_CLASSES_FACTOR_THROUGH_SIX_PHYSICAL_CONTENT_BUCKETS / PROVED_SIX_BUCKETS_PAIRWISE_COPRIME / PROVED_THREE_SPLIT_ONLY_HYPOTENUSE_BUCKETS / PROVED_ODD_SUPPORT_DISJOINTNESS_OF_DELTA0_DELTA_PLUS_DELTA_MINUS / PROVED_TWIST_ODD_SUPPORT_COPRIME_TO_BASE_HILBERT_ODD_SUPPORT / SELECTOR_CONDITIONED_COUNT_STILL_OPEN / PREFERRED_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229AC EXACT SELECTOR-HILBERT PACKET / NESTED PYTHAGOREAN CONTENT FACTORIZATION / ODD-PRIME SUPPORT LOCALIZATION / THEOREM-INPUT SHARPENING


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AC
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
CARD_DOC_ID: 1byAfUpYWBOHo6jQhrkD5faNZUytMNi7UmLp6PH_YS3Q


1. Scope


229M explicitly resolved the two selector Hilbert squareclasses delta_+, delta_- into physical Pythagorean gap/content data and used their product to identify the moving congruent-number twist.
229N/O then collapsed that product to
  G_* = gcd(eR,xy),
  d_tw = sf(2^epsilon G_*).


The base norm-square condition N(p) square also has its own rational Hilbert squareclass delta_0 from229L:
  p = delta_0 s_0^2,
  p^2+1 = delta_+ s_+^2,
  p^2-1 = delta_- s_-^2,
with delta_j in Q^* and s_j in Q(i)^*.


Until now Stage37 did not push delta_0 through the same physical content crosswalk. This card does so and proves that the three rational squareclasses split, away from2, into six mutually coprime physical content buckets.


No endpoint power saving is claimed.


2. Retained exact physical factorization


Use229D notation but rename its common missing-face content d as d0 to avoid collision with the canonical elliptic twist.


The exact four-chart/nested factorization is
  e = g a b,
  x = d0 b c,
  y = d0 a f,                                    (229AD.1)
with
  gcd(a,b)=1,
  gcd(c,f)=1,
  gcd(g,d0)=1,
  gcd(g,c)=gcd(g,f)=1,
  gcd(a,d0)=gcd(a,c)=1,
  gcd(b,d0)=gcd(b,f)=1.


The missing-face primitive triple is
  (b c)^2 + (a f)^2 = q^2,
  z=d0 q,                                        (229AD.2)
with
  gcd(bc,af)=1,
  q odd,
  gcd(q,abcf)=1.


Set
  h=gcd(e,z)=gcd(g,q).                            (229AD.3)
Then
  h|g,
  h|q,
  gcd(h,d0abcf)=1,
and every prime divisor of h is 1 mod4.


The two primitive face triples are
  (g a, d0 c, n1),
  (g b, d0 f, n2),                               (229AD.4)
with
  U=b n1,
  V=a n2.


Retain229M:
  c12=gcd(U,y)=gcd(n1,f),
  c21=gcd(V,x)=gcd(n2,c).                        (229AD.5)


3. Explicit base Hilbert squareclass delta_0


Retain229J:
  p=((x+i y)(R+e))/z^2,
  v=(R+e)/z,
  N(p)=v^2.                                      (229AD.6)


Because x,y>0, p is non-real, so the exact Hilbert-class lemma229M.1 applies to zeta=p:
if N(p)=v^2 then the rational squareclass of p is represented by
  2v+Tr(p).


Now
  Tr(p)=2x(R+e)/z^2,
hence
  2v+Tr(p)
    =2(R+e)/z + 2x(R+e)/z^2
    =2(R+e)(z+x)/z^2.                            (229AD.7)


The denominator z^2 is a rational square, so
  [delta_0]=[2(R+e)(z+x)].                       (229AD.8)


Use
  (R+e)(R-e)=z^2,
  (z+x)(z-x)=y^2.
Therefore
  [R+e]=[R-e],
  [z+x]=[z-x]
in Q^*/Q^{*2}, and
  [delta_0]=[2(R-e)(z-x)].                       (229AD.9)


RESULT_229AD_BASE_HILBERT_CLASS_PHYSICAL_GAP_FORMULA=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Apply the Pythagorean gap-squareclass lemma


Retain229M.2:
for a positive integral Pythagorean triple
  A^2+B^2=C^2
with content m,
  [C-A] is [m] or [2m]
depending only on the primitive-leg parity.


Apply it first to
  (e,z,R),
whose content is h by (229AD.3):
  [R-e]=[2^{r0} h],  r0 in {0,1}.                (229AD.10)


Apply it to
  (x,y,z),
whose content is d0:
  [z-x]=[2^{s0} d0], s0 in {0,1}.                (229AD.11)


Combining with (229AD.9), there exists
  epsilon_0 in {0,1}
such that
  [delta_0]=[2^{epsilon_0} h d0].                (229AD.12)


This is the exact missing third-content crosswalk.


RESULT_229AD_DELTA0_EQUALS_HD0_UP_TO_2ADIC_BIT=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Put delta_+, delta_- in the same packet


Retain229M:
  [delta_+]=[(U-e)(R-U)],
  [delta_-]=[(V-e)(R-V)].                        (229AD.13)


The triples
  (e,x,U),
  (U,y,R)
have contents b,c12 respectively, so the same gap lemma gives
  [delta_+]=[2^{epsilon_+} b c12],
  epsilon_+ in {0,1}.                            (229AD.14)


The triples
  (e,y,V),
  (V,x,R)
have contents a,c21 respectively, hence
  [delta_-]=[2^{epsilon_-} a c21],
  epsilon_- in {0,1}.                            (229AD.15)


Thus the three rational Hilbert classes have the uniform physical packet


  delta_0 : h * d0,
  delta_+ : b * c12,
  delta_- : a * c21,                             (229AD.16)


up to independent harmless 2-adic parity bits.


RESULT_229AD_THREE_HILBERT_CLASS_CONTENT_PACKET=PROVED_EXACT.


The canonical twist remains
  d_tw=sf(delta_+ delta_-)
      =sf(2^epsilon a b c12 c21),                (229AD.17)
consistent with229M/N/O.


6. The six physical content buckets are pairwise coprime


We prove pairwise coprimality for
  h, d0, a, b, c12, c21.                         (229AD.18)


From229D,
  gcd(h,d0abcf)=1,
so h is coprime to d0,a,b and, because c12|f and c21|c, also to c12,c21.


Also from229D,
  gcd(d0,a)=gcd(d0,b)=1.


Because c12|n1 and (ga,d0c,n1) is primitive,
  gcd(c12,d0)=gcd(c12,a)=1.
Because c12|f and gcd(b,f)=1,
  gcd(c12,b)=1.


Similarly c21|n2 and (gb,d0f,n2) primitive give
  gcd(c21,d0)=gcd(c21,b)=1,
while c21|c and gcd(a,c)=1 give
  gcd(c21,a)=1.


Finally
  c12|f,
  c21|c,
  gcd(c,f)=1,
so
  gcd(c12,c21)=1.


Together with gcd(a,b)=1, all six entries in (229AD.18) are pairwise coprime.


RESULT_229AD_SIX_CONTENT_BUCKETS_PAIRWISE_COPRIME=PROVED_EXACT.


Consequently the odd-prime supports of delta_0, delta_+, delta_- are pairwise disjoint:
  supp_odd(delta_0)=supp(h) disjoint-union supp(d0),
  supp_odd(delta_+)=supp(b) disjoint-union supp(c12),
  supp_odd(delta_-)=supp(a) disjoint-union supp(c21).  (229AD.19)


In particular,
  gcd( oddpart(delta_0), oddpart(d_tw) )=1.       (229AD.20)


RESULT_229AD_THREE_HILBERT_ODD_SUPPORTS_PAIRWISE_DISJOINT=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AD_BASE_CLASS_ODD_SUPPORT_COPRIME_TO_TWIST_ODD_SUPPORT=PROVED_EXACT.


7. Three of the six buckets are split-prime only


The integer q is the hypotenuse of the primitive Pythagorean triple (bc,af,q), so every odd prime divisor of q is 1 mod4.
Since h|q,
  p|h => p=1 mod4 for every odd p.                (229AD.21)


Likewise n1,n2 are hypotenuses of the primitive face triples in (229AD.4). Therefore every odd prime divisor of n1 or n2 is 1 mod4.
Since
  c12|n1,
  c21|n2,
we have
  p|c12 c21 => p=1 mod4 for every odd p.         (229AD.22)


Thus the six-bucket packet has an alternating structure:


  unrestricted leg/common-content buckets:
    d0, b, a;


  Gaussian-split hypotenuse-overlap buckets:
    h, c12, c21,
    supported only on odd primes p=1 mod4.        (229AD.23)


RESULT_229AD_H_C12_C21_SPLIT_PRIME_SUPPORT=PROVED_EXACT.


A useful corollary for the preferred twist radical is:
every odd prime p=3 mod4 dividing
  K_*=sf(gcd(eR,xy))
must lie in a or b, hence in the e-side content
  A_edge=ab=gcd(e,xy).                            (229AD.24)


Equivalently, the odd 3 mod4 support of the R-side content
  C_raw=c12 c21
is empty.


RESULT_229AD_INERT_PRIME_TWIST_SUPPORT_LOCALIZED_TO_E_SIDE=PROVED_EXACT.


8. Relation to the preferred radical gate


Retain229O:
  G_*=gcd(eR,xy)=a b c12 c21,
  K_*=sf(G_*).                                    (229AD.25)


229AD does not make K_* small. It refines its arithmetic support:
- the twist packet delta_+ and delta_- have disjoint odd support;
- each packet contains exactly one unrestricted content bucket and one split-only bucket;
- the unused base Hilbert class delta_0 is odd-coprime to the twist support and itself has the same unrestricted/split-only pattern.


Therefore the selector-conditioned theorem input can be stated more sharply than “count arbitrary twists d”:


count physical packets
  (kappa_0,kappa_+,kappa_-)
with
  kappa_0=sf(2^{e0} h d0),
  kappa_+=sf(2^{e+} b c12),
  kappa_-=sf(2^{e-} a c21),                      (229AD.26)
whose odd parts are pairwise coprime, whose h,c12,c21 prime support is entirely split in Q(i), and which arise from the exact nested primitive Pythagorean system and physical height R<=B.


The preferred twist is
  d_tw=sf(kappa_+ kappa_-).


RESULT_229AD_SELECTOR_CONDITIONED_THEOREM_INTERFACE=THREE_PAIRWISE_ODD_COPRIME_HILBERT_PACKETS_WITH_SPLIT_SUPPORT_HALF_BUCKETS.


9. What this does not prove


No fixed-power saving follows solely from support localization.


The sectors
  h=1,
  c12=1,
  c21=1
are all arithmetically allowed by the retained exact parameterization, so the split-only factors may disappear entirely.
The unrestricted buckets d0,a,b can still carry arbitrary odd prime support subject to the existing physical equations.


Therefore:
  PHYSICAL_JOINT_RADICAL_GCD_ONE_THIRD remains OPEN.
  CM_PAIR_INDEPENDENT_BRANCH remains OPEN.
  GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT remains0.


The result is a theorem-interface sharpening, not a numerator bound.


10. Route consequence


The generic-rank route remains HOLD by229AC.


The highest-value next input is now one of:


(A) THREE_PACKET_SELECTOR_SUPPORT_COUNT:
a same-physical theorem counting the exact packet (kappa_0,kappa_+,kappa_-) of (229AD.26), preserving pairwise odd coprimality, the split-only h/c12/c21 supports, and the exact R-height, with o(B^{1/3}) large-twist output;


(B) TWO_PACKET_TWIST_SUPPORT_COUNT:
a theorem directly counting kappa_+,kappa_- under their disjoint odd support and one-split-one-unrestricted bucket structure, strong enough to control
  sf(kappa_+ kappa_-)>B^{1/3-delta};


(C) DIRECT_SAME_PHYSICAL_RADICAL_SUPPORT:
the existing preferred theorem for
  sf(gcd(eR,xy));


(D) any sharper physical twist cutoff or selector-aware two-point theorem meeting the already recorded229AC exponent contracts.


DO_NOT_CONTINUE:
- do not treat split-prime support alone as a power saving;
- do not discard delta_0: it is now an exact third rational squareclass packet, although it is not part of d_tw;
- do not merge the six buckets and lose their pairwise-coprime structure before theorem matching;
- do not reopen generic rank>=2 statistics without229AC's gamma<1/6 equivalent;
- do not reopen CM dependence unless229AB fails audit.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.

11. Verification scope


This is a within-session exact algebra/content deduction from retained229D/J/L/M/N/O. It is not an independent hostile audit of those cards.


Load-bearing checks:
- explicit Hilbert-class representative 2r+Tr(zeta) from229M.1;
- p=((x+iy)(R+e))/z^2 and N(p)=((R+e)/z)^2 from229J;
- nested factorization e=gab, x=d0bc, y=d0af, z=d0q and h=gcd(g,q) from229D;
- face hypotenuses n1,n2 and c12=gcd(n1,f), c21=gcd(n2,c) from229M;
- Pythagorean gap-squareclass lemma229M.2;
- quotient-free twist radical G_*=gcd(eR,xy) from229O.


No new external theorem is used.

Internal:

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AC — CM independent-pair regulator identity and generic rank-two theorem budget firewall


STATUS: POST_229AB_CM_INDEPENDENT_PAIR_AUDIT / PROVED_EXACT_CM_PAIR_GRAM_DETERMINANT / PROVED_INDEPENDENT_BRANCH_RANK_GE_2_SMALL_PAIR_ROUTING / PROVED_SMITH_THEOREM_SPECIES_APPLIES_TO_CONGRUENT_BASE_CURVE / SMITH_RANK_GE_2_oX_TOO_WEAK_AT_d_LE_2B2_SCALE / TWO_SELMER_DISTRIBUTION_NOT_A_ONE_THIRD_COUNT / PETIT_DETERMINANT_METHOD_BLACK_BOX_MISMATCH_AND_IDEALIZED_EXPONENT_TOO_WEAK / GENERIC_RANK_STATISTICS_ROUTE_HOLD / PREFERRED_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229AB CM-INDEPENDENT-PAIR STRUCTURAL REDUCTION / NERON-TATE GRAM IDENTITY / GENERIC RANK-TWO THEOREM BUDGET AUDIT / DETERMINANT-METHOD FIREWALL


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AB
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
CARD_DOC_ID: 1XPPSxaG_j0Pu-lwJ2TjRSdeIfbKmfOsssmFqHe-2rso


1. Scope


229AB closes the CM-pair DEPENDENCE locus on the preferred large-radical tail:
  dependent endpoints = B^{o(1)}=o(B^{1/3}).
The remaining CM route is therefore the physical population for which
  A=P+sigma(P),
  C=iota(P-sigma(P))
are independent modulo E_d(Q)_tors.


This card does two things:
(1) compresses independence into one exact Neron-Tate Gram-determinant condition tied directly to the physical point P;
(2) audits the strongest generic rank>=2 / two-small-point theorem species found against the exact Stage37 d<=2B^2 and B^(1/3) budget.


The result is a route firewall, not a closure of the independent branch.


2. Exact CM pair Gram determinant


Work on
  E_d: Y^2=X^3-d^2X,
  K=Q(i),
with complex conjugation sigma and CM automorphism
  iota=[i],  iota(X,Y)=(-X,iY).


Use the symmetric Neron-Tate bilinear pairing
  <Q1,Q2>
with
  <Q,Q>=hhat(Q).


Put
  H=hhat(P),
  T=<P,sigma(P)>,
  U=<P,iota sigma(P)>.


Retain229R:
  A=P+sigma(P) in E_d(Q),
  C=iota(P-sigma(P)) in E_d(Q),
  hhat(A)+hhat(C)=4H.                            (229AC.1)


Under the principal polarization the Rosati adjoint of iota=[i] is
  iota^dagger=[-i].
Hence
  <Q,iota Q>=0                                   (229AC.2)
for every Q, because symmetry and the adjoint identity give
  <Q,iota Q>=<iota^dagger Q,Q>=<-iota Q,Q>=-<Q,iota Q>.


Therefore
  hhat(A)=2H+2T,
  hhat(C)=2H-2T.                                 (229AC.3)


For the cross term,
  <A,C>
   =<P+sigma P, iota P-iota sigma P>
   =-2U.                                         (229AC.4)


Thus the exact Gram determinant of the rational CM pair is


  Delta_CM(P)
   := det [[hhat(A), <A,C>],
           [<A,C>, hhat(C)]]
    =4(H^2-T^2-U^2).                             (229AC.5)


RESULT_229AC_CM_PAIR_GRAM_DETERMINANT=PROVED_EXACT.


Because the Neron-Tate form is positive definite on E_d(Q)/torsion,
  Delta_CM(P)=0
iff A,C are dependent modulo torsion,
and
  Delta_CM(P)>0
iff A,C are independent modulo torsion.          (229AC.6)


Combined with229AB, the Delta_CM(P)=0 physical locus on the preferred large-radical tail is B^{o(1)}.


RESULT_229AC_DEPENDENCE_EQUALS_ZERO_GRAM_LOCUS=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AC_INDEPENDENT_BRANCH_EQUALS_POSITIVE_GRAM_LOCUS=PROVED_EXACT.


3. What the independent branch gives exactly


On the surviving independent branch:
- A and C are independent non-torsion points in E_d(Q);
- therefore rank E_d(Q)>=2;
- their total canonical height is not arbitrary but
    hhat(A)+hhat(C)=4hhat(P)=O(log B),            (229AC.7)
  using retained229L/229R;
- the pair comes from the distinguished physical Gaussian selector/descent packet, not from an arbitrary rank-two twist.


Thus the exact theorem target is substantially thinner than generic rank>=2 support:
count squarefree d and physical pairs (A,C) with
  rank span{A,C}=2,
  hhat(A)+hhat(C)=O(log B),
  Delta_CM(P)>0,
plus the inherited selector/radical realization.


RESULT_229AC_INDEPENDENT_BRANCH_RANK2_SMALL_PAIR_ROUTING=PROVED_EXACT.


No lower bound for Delta_CM(P) beyond positivity is proved. In particular, no regulator saving is claimed from (229AC.5) alone.


4. Smith 2-infinity-Selmer theorem applies to the base twist family


The fixed base curve
  E: y^2=x^3-x
has full rational 2-torsion.


It also has no rational cyclic subgroup of order4. Indeed the duplication formula is
  x(2Q)=(x(Q)^2+1)^2/[4x(Q)(x(Q)^2-1)].
Halving the three rational 2-torsion points would require respectively
  x(Q)=+/-i,
  x(Q)=1+/-sqrt(2),
  x(Q)=-1+/-sqrt(2),
so no order-four cyclic subgroup is Galois-stable over Q.


The quadratic twist model
  d y^2=x^3-x
is Q-isomorphic to the Stage37 congruent-number model
  Y^2=X^3-d^2X
via
  X=d x,  Y=d^2 y.                               (229AC.8)


Therefore Alexander Smith's theorem species applies: among squarefree twists |d|<X, the number with Mordell-Weil rank at least2 is o(X).


RESULT_229AC_SMITH_RANK2_THEOREM_SPECIES=APPLICABLE_TO_BASE_TWIST_FAMILY.


But this is quantitatively insufficient for Stage37. Retain
  d<=2B^2
and the uniform fixed-d endpoint fiber B^{o(1)} from229L.
An o(X) rank-two support theorem at X asymptotic to B^2 yields only
  o(B^2)*B^{o(1)},
which does NOT imply o(B^{1/3}).


RESULT_229AC_SMITH_oX_DIRECT_STAGE37_MATCH=NO_GO_AT_CURRENT_TWIST_SCALE.


5. Exact exponent contract for any generic rank-two support theorem


Suppose a future generic theorem gives
  R_2(X):=#{squarefree d<=X: rank E_d(Q)>=2}
    << X^{gamma+o(1)}.                            (229AC.9)


At the current Stage37 envelope X~B^2, retained229L gives
  independent physical endpoints
    << B^{2gamma+o(1)}.                           (229AC.10)


To beat the one-third budget one needs
  2gamma<1/3,
i.e.
  gamma<1/6.                                      (229AC.11)


Equivalently, a bound R_2(X)<<X^{1-eta+o(1)} requires
  eta>5/6.


RESULT_229AC_GENERIC_RANK2_REQUIRED_EXPONENT=gamma<1/6.
RESULT_229AC_GENERIC_RANK2_REQUIRED_SAVING=eta>5/6.


This is a method-level necessary threshold under the current d<=2B^2 envelope and fixed-d B^{o(1)} fiber. It is not a lower bound on the true physical population.


6. Two-Selmer distribution is not the missing count


Modern distribution theorems for full-rational-2-torsion twist families determine positive-density distributions of 2-Selmer ranks.


But
  rank E_d(Q) <= dim Sel_2(E_d)-dim E_d(Q)[2],
so using a high 2-Selmer-rank condition as an upper envelope for rank>=2 leaves positive-density Selmer strata. Such information alone supplies no X^{gamma} upper bound with gamma<1, much less the required gamma<1/6.


Smith's 2-infinity-Selmer theorem is stronger because it gives actual rank>=2 support o(X), but Section4 shows even that is far too weak at X~B^2.


RESULT_229AC_TWO_SELMER_DISTRIBUTION_ALONE=NO_GO_FOR_ONE_THIRD_BUDGET.


7. Petit determinant-method two-small-point route: contract mismatch


Joachim Petit's second-moment method is much closer in shape to the Stage37 independent-pair problem: it controls off-diagonal pairs of small rational points on the same quadratic twist by a determinant-method estimate.


However the theorem is not a black-box match.


First mismatch: Petit's setup assumes
  F(x,z)=x^3+A x z^2+B z^3
is irreducible over Z, equivalently the base curve has trivial rational 2-torsion in the relevant line-locus argument. Stage37 has
  F(x,z)=x^3-x z^2=x(x-z)(x+z),
with full rational 2-torsion.


In Petit's proof irreducibility is used to identify rational points on the line locus of the determinant-method surface with the excluded diagonal. For the congruent-number curve extra line components must be re-audited; the theorem cannot simply be quoted.


Second mismatch: Petit's almost-minimal regime requires the small-point parameter alpha<1/120. Stage37 currently has only the coarse physical adapter hhat(P)=O(log B) and no theorem placing both A,C uniformly in Petit's near-minimal d^{1/8+alpha} window.


RESULT_229AC_PETIT_BLACKBOX_APPLICABILITY=NO.


8. Even an idealized Petit transfer misses the Stage37 exponent


Petit's off-diagonal determinant-method term has the exponent
  X^{13/32+45 alpha/4+epsilon}.                  (229AC.12)


Ignore, counterfactually, both mismatches of Section7 and grant the same exponent directly to the relevant physical independent-pair support.


At alpha tending to 0, the best power is
  gamma_Petit=13/32.


With X~B^2 this becomes
  B^{13/16+o(1)},                                (229AC.13)
still far above B^{1/3}.


More generally, if an independent argument first improved the twist envelope to
  d<=B^beta,
the idealized Petit exponent would meet the one-third target only if
  beta(13/32+45 alpha/4)<1/3.                    (229AC.14)


In the optimistic alpha->0 limit this requires
  beta<32/39 approximately 0.8205128.            (229AC.15)


Current beta=2 is far outside this range.


RESULT_229AC_PETIT_IDEALIZED_CURRENT_SCALE=NO_GO.
RESULT_229AC_PETIT_OPTIMISTIC_TWIST_CUTOFF_THRESHOLD=beta<32/39.


For comparison, retained229Q's one-small-point Le Boudec route needs the even stronger optimistic cutoff beta<2/3. Neither cutoff is currently available.


9. Route consequence


The 229AB closure materially changes the logic: dependence is no longer the obstruction. But generic rank>=2 statistics do not become sufficient merely because independence is now available.


CM_PAIR_INDEPENDENT_BRANCH remains OPEN.


The generic route
  physical independent pair
    -> forget selectors and count all rank>=2 twists
is now placed on
  HOLD_NO_GO_AT_CURRENT_d_LE_2B2_SCALE,
because:
- Smith gives actual rank>=2 support only o(X), with no Stage37-sufficient power;
- 2-Selmer distribution is too broad;
- Petit's two-small-point determinant method is not directly applicable to full rational 2-torsion and, even under an idealized transfer of its best exponent, gives B^{13/16+o(1)} at the current twist scale.


RESULT_229AC_GENERIC_CM_INDEPENDENT_PAIR_RANK_STATISTICS_ROUTE=HOLD_NO_GO_AT_CURRENT_SCALE.


The preferred whole-population gate remains unchanged:
  #{positive primitive physical endpoints R_phys<=B:
      sf(gcd(e R_phys, x y))>B^(1/3-delta)}
    =o(B^(1/3))
for some fixed delta>0.


GAUSSIAN_TWIST_RADICAL_GCD remains CONDITIONAL_RESERVE/THEOREM_WATCH.


10. Next useful input


NEXT_USEFUL_INPUT:
(A) DIRECT_SAME_PHYSICAL_RADICAL_SUPPORT theorem for sf(gcd(eR,xy)), still preferred;
(B) SELECTOR_CONDITIONED_CM_INDEPENDENT_PAIR theorem that retains the physical Gaussian/2-descent/radical structure and proves o(B^(1/3)) directly, rather than passing through all rank>=2 twists;
(C) a genuinely sharper physical twist bound d<=B^beta. For the idealized Petit-type exponent alone one would need beta<32/39, together with a new full-2-torsion/off-diagonal adaptation and the near-minimal-height contract;
(D) another support-level theorem giving the same one-third budget.


DO_NOT_CONTINUE:
- do not reopen CM dependence unless229AB fails audit;
- do not iterate generic rank>=2 density/Selmer theorems without an explicit gamma<1/6 equivalent at the current twist scale;
- do not treat Petit's irreducible-cubic theorem as directly applicable to x^3-x;
- do not infer a regulator lower bound from Delta_CM(P)>0 alone.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.


Integrated audit186-229O remains unchanged in scope and is not silently extended to229P-229AC.


11. Verification scope


This is a within-session exact CM-pair identity plus external theorem-contract/budget audit. It is not an independent hostile audit of229P-229AC.


Load-bearing internal checks:
- Rosati adjoint [i]^dagger=[-i];
- exact 229R definitions of A,C and height sum;
- positive definiteness of the Neron-Tate pairing modulo torsion;
- 229AB dependence locus already B^{o(1)};
- 229L fixed-d endpoint fiber B^{o(1)};
- current exact twist envelope d<=2B^2 from retained229Q/229M-N-O chain.


External theorem use is scoped only to theorem species and exponent budgets below.


12. Sources checked


Internal:
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AB;
- 229R exact CM pair and height identity;
- 229Q small-point twist budget ceiling;
- 229L congruent-number router / physical height / fixed-d B^{o(1)};
- current MAIN / CARD-INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active ROUTE.


External:
- Alexander Smith, “2^infinity-Selmer groups, 2^infinity-class groups, and Goldfeld's conjecture”, arXiv:1702.02325. Used for actual rank>=2 support o(X) under full rational 2-torsion/no rational cyclic order4.
- Jinzhao Pan and Ye Tian, “On the Distribution of 2-Selmer ranks of Quadratic Twists of Elliptic Curves over Q”, arXiv:2503.21462. Used only for the current full-2-torsion 2-Selmer distribution theorem species / positive-density Selmer-strata firewall.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AB — uniform primitive even-CM ramified pullback and total CM-dependence closure


STATUS: POST_229AA_UNIFORM_EVEN_CM_RAMIFIED_THEOREM / PROVED_PRIMITIVE_EVEN_SLOPE_HAS_EXACTLY_ONE_RAMIFIED_FACTOR / PROVED_UNIFORM_TORSION_FREE_RAMIFIED_PULLBACK / PROVED_TWO_FIXED_SMOOTH_GENUS_NALPHA_MINUS_3_RECEIVERS / PROVED_ALL_BOUNDED_EVEN_CM_DEPENDENCE_Bo1 / CM_PAIR_DEPENDENCE_SUBGATE_CLOSED_FOR_ONE_THIRD_BUDGET / GLOBAL_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229AA UNIFORM EVEN CM RAMIFIED-FACTOR THEOREM / FIXED HYPERELLIPTIC RECEIVER CLASSIFICATION / TOTAL CM-DEPENDENCE CLOSURE


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AA
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
CARD_DOC_ID: 1l-CMX--br4H9Q63Z62TosJsxjCaSyP3kClq0JLQF3p0


1. Scope


229AA closes every primitive ODD Gaussian dependence slope in the bounded 229S slope set. The remaining dependence problem was primitive EVEN slopes of norm >10; norm2 is physically empty and norm10 was closed explicitly by229X.


This card proves that the norm10 mechanism is not exceptional. Every primitive even Gaussian slope contains exactly one ramified factor 1+i, and after removing it the remaining factor is primitive odd. The uniform odd divisor theorem229AA then supplies a fixed genus>1 receiver on BOTH ramified sign branches. Therefore all bounded even slopes are B^{o(1)}, and the entire CM-pair DEPENDENCE subgate is closed for the Stage37 one-third budget.


This does NOT count the independent CM-pair branch and does NOT close the preferred whole-population radical-gcd gate.


2. Primitive even Gaussian slopes have exactly one ramified factor


Retain229S. A dependent physical point has a primitive Gaussian slope
  alpha=a-ib in Z[i],
  gcd(a,b)=1, ab!=0,
and
  2P=[alpha]R+T,
  R in E_d(Q) non-torsion,
  T in E_d[2].


Assume N(alpha)=a^2+b^2 is even. Since gcd(a,b)=1, a and b must both be odd. Hence
  alpha=(1+i) beta
up to a Gaussian unit/conjugation, and v_{1+i}(alpha)=1: divisibility by (1+i)^2=2i would force both a and b even.


Write
  n=N(beta)=N(alpha)/2.
Then n is odd. The Gaussian integer beta is primitive: any common odd rational divisor of its integer coordinates would divide a and b after multiplication by 1+i, and both coordinates cannot be even because n is odd.


If one coordinate of beta vanished, primitivity would force N(alpha)=2. Thus for every primitive even slope with N(alpha)>2, beta is primitive odd with both coordinates nonzero and n>=5.


RESULT_229AB_PRIMITIVE_EVEN_FACTORIZATION=PROVED_EXACT:
  alpha=(unit)*(1+i)*beta,
  beta primitive odd,
  N(beta)=N(alpha)/2,
  with exactly one ramified factor.


Norm2 remains physically empty by229S.


3. Uniform torsion-free ramified representative


Start from
  2P=[(1+i)beta]R+T.                              (229AB.1)


Multiply by 1-i:
  2[1-i]P=2[beta]R+[1-i]T.


Set
  X=[1-i]P-[beta]R.
Then
  [2]X=[1-i]T,
so X is K=Q(i)-torsion. Retain the 229Q torsion firewall on the physical squarefree twists d>1:
  E_d(K)_tors=E_d[2].
Therefore [2]X=0. Hence [1-i]T=0 and X=S lies in E_d[2].


Because beta has odd norm, [beta] acts bijectively on E_d[2]. Choose S' in E_d[2] with [beta]S'=S and replace R by R'=R+S'. Then
  [1-i]P=[beta]R',
  R' in E_d(Q).                                  (229AB.2)


This is exactly the 229V ramified-factor reduction, now with arbitrary primitive odd beta.


RESULT_229AB_UNIFORM_RAMIFIED_TORSION_REDUCTION=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Uniform squareclass crosswalk


Write the physical normalized coordinate
  z_P=X(P)/d=p^2 in K^{*2},
and put
  s=X([1-i]P)/d.


Retain the exact 229V map
  s=i(z_P^2-1)/(2z_P).                            (229AB.3)


The retained 229L physical selector squareclasses imply
  [s]=[d] in K^*/K^{*2}.                         (229AB.4)


On the other hand, R' is rational. Put
  r=X(R')/d in Q.
By229AA/229W for the primitive odd beta,
  X([beta]R')/X(R')=H_beta(r)^2
with H_beta in K(X)^*. Hence from (229AB.2),
  s=r H_beta(r)^2,
so
  [s]=[r] in K^*/K^{*2}.                         (229AB.5)


For rational r,d, the kernel of
  Q^*/Q^{*2} -> K^*/K^{*2}
is generated by -1. Therefore
  r=epsilon*d*t^2,
  epsilon in {+1,-1},
  t in Q^*.                                      (229AB.6)


Exactly as in229V, the rational point R' gives
  w^2=epsilon(q^2-1),
  q=d*t^2>0.                                     (229AB.7)


Thus the raw ramified carrier is always one of the same two conics as norm10. This part is independent of beta.


RESULT_229AB_UNIFORM_RAMIFIED_SQUARECLASS_CROSSWALK=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Coprime pullback removes the ramified division


Because beta has odd norm,
  gcd_{Z[i]}(beta,1-i)=1.
Choose A,B in Z[i] with
  A beta+B(1-i)=1.


Define
  Q=[A]P+[B]R'.
Using (229AB.2),
  [1-i]Q=R'.                                     (229AB.8)


Also
  [1-i](P-[beta]Q)=0,
so
  P=[beta]Q+S,
  S in ker[1-i]={O,T0},
  T0=(0,0).                                      (229AB.9)


For odd beta, [beta]T0=T0. If S=T0, replace Q by Q+T0. Since [1-i]T0=O, equation (229AB.8) is unchanged, while [beta](Q+T0)=[beta]Q+T0=P.


Therefore every primitive even dependence point admits an exact representative
  [1-i]Q=R' in E_d(Q),
  P=[beta]Q,                                     (229AB.10)
with no residual torsion.


RESULT_229AB_UNIFORM_COPRIME_PULLBACK=PROVED_EXACT.


6. Physical square condition forces the ramified preimage X-coordinate to be a K-square


Put
  z=X(Q)/d in K.


Retain229AA:
  X([beta]Q)/X(Q)=H_beta(z)^2,
where
  H_beta(z)=c_beta A_beta(z)/B_beta(z),
  deg A_beta=deg B_beta=(n-1)/2,
and A_beta,B_beta are squarefree and coprime.


By (229AB.10),
  X(P)/d=z H_beta(z)^2.
The physical condition X(P)/d=p^2 therefore forces
  z=s0^2 in K^{*2}.                              (229AB.11)


One can take
  p=+/- s0 H_beta(z).
Thus the remaining physical base condition
  N_{K/Q}(p) in Q^{*2}
is exactly
  N(s0) N(H_beta(z)) in Q^{*2}.                  (229AB.12)


RESULT_229AB_RAMIFIED_PREIMAGE_X_IS_K_SQUARE=PROVED_EXACT.


7. The two ramified sign branches are degree-two pullbacks


The relation [1-i]Q=R' gives the same normalized map as229X:
  r=i(z^2-1)/(2z).                               (229AB.13)


PLUS branch epsilon=+1:
  r=q=d t^2.
Solving (229AB.13) gives z=i h with h=-q+/-sqrt(q^2-1), the two choices reciprocal. Since z is a K-square and h is rational negative on the nonboundary real branch,
  h=-2a^2,
  a in Q^*,
so
  z_+(a)=-2 i a^2.                               (229AB.14)


Choose s0=a(1-i). Then N(s0)=2a^2, a rational square times the fixed constant2. Hence (229AB.12), modulo a rational square, is
  2*N(H_beta(z_+(a))) in Q^{*2}.                 (229AB.15)


MINUS branch epsilon=-1:
  r=-q.
The conic gives N(z)=1. Since z=s0^2, choose the standard rational norm-one parameter
  s0=(u-i)/(u+i),
  u in Q,
so
  z_-(u)=((u-i)/(u+i))^2.                        (229AB.16)


Here N(s0)=1, and (229AB.12) is
  N(H_beta(z_-(u))) in Q^{*2}.                   (229AB.17)


Thus for every fixed beta, each sign branch is a fixed double cover of a rational parameter line.


8. Uniform support separation on the PLUS branch


Retain229AA:
  H_beta(z)=c A(z)/B(z),
where m=(n-1)/2,
- A and B are squarefree degree m;
- their roots are finite, nonzero, non-2-torsion X-values;
- the zero/pole supports for beta and bar(beta) are separated by Gaussian coprimality.


For rational a,
  bar(z_+(a))=-z_+(a).
Therefore the norm in (229AB.15) has zero/pole factors coming from
  A(z), B(z), bar(A)(-z), bar(B)(-z).            (229AB.18)


Geometrically, for a point Q_z with normalized X-coordinate z:
  A(z)=0        <=> [beta]Q_z=T0,
  B(z)=0        <=> [beta]Q_z=O,
  bar(A)(-z)=0 <=> [i bar(beta)]Q_z=T0,
  bar(B)(-z)=0 <=> [i bar(beta)]Q_z=O.           (229AB.19)


Because beta is primitive odd,
  gcd(beta,i bar(beta))=1
in Z[i]. A Bezout combination shows that any collision between a beta support and an i bar(beta) support forces Q_z into E_d[2]. The only possible O/T0 points are precisely the canceled points excluded from the finite A/B supports; the other 2-torsion points cannot map to O or T0 in the required way under odd beta.


Hence all four support sets in (229AB.18) are pairwise disjoint and simple.


The map a -> z_+(a) has degree2 and is ramified only over z=0,infinity. Those values are absent from the 229AA finite zero/pole supports. Therefore every support point has two simple preimages.


Each of the four X-line support sets has m points, hence the PLUS parameter-line squareclass has exactly
  4*(2m)=4(n-1)
simple branch points.                               (229AB.20)


RESULT_229AB_PLUS_BRANCH_SUPPORT_SQUAREFREE=PROVED_EXACT.


9. Uniform support separation on the MINUS branch


For rational u,
  bar(z_-(u))=1/z_-(u).                           (229AB.21)


On E_d, normalized X-coordinate inversion z -> 1/z is induced by the automorphism
  psi(Q)=[i](Q+T0):
translation by T0 sends z to -1/z and [i] sends normalized X to its negative.


Hence the norm in (229AB.17) has factors
  A(z), B(z), bar(A)(1/z), bar(B)(1/z).          (229AB.22)


Let phi=[i bar(beta)]. Since beta has odd norm, beta and bar(beta) fix T0, and [i] fixes T0. Therefore:
  bar(A)(1/z)=0 <=> phi Q_z=O,
  bar(B)(1/z)=0 <=> phi Q_z=T0.                  (229AB.23)


Together with
  A(z)=0 <=> [beta]Q_z=T0,
  B(z)=0 <=> [beta]Q_z=O,
and gcd(beta,phi)=1, Bezout again forces every cross-collision into E_d[2]. The canceled O/T0 cases are not finite A/B roots, and the remaining 2-torsion points cannot satisfy the required images. Thus the four support sets are pairwise disjoint and simple.


The map u -> z_-(u) has degree2 and is ramified only above z=0,infinity, again disjoint from the 229AA supports. Hence every support point has two simple preimages and the MINUS parameter-line squareclass also has exactly
  4(n-1)
simple branch points.                              (229AB.24)


RESULT_229AB_MINUS_BRANCH_SUPPORT_SQUAREFREE=PROVED_EXACT.


10. Uniform fixed-curve genus for every primitive even slope


For either sign branch, after clearing an even denominator the physical norm-square condition defines a fixed hyperelliptic curve over Q whose squareclass branch divisor consists of exactly
  D=4(n-1)
distinct geometric points.


Since D is even, the smooth projective model has genus
  g=(D-2)/2
   =2n-3
   =N(alpha)-3.                                  (229AB.25)


For every surviving primitive even slope N(alpha)>2, n>=5, so
  g>=7.


This recovers the explicit norm10 result229X:
  N(alpha)=10 -> n=5 -> g=7.


RESULT_229AB_UNIFORM_EVEN_SELECTOR_CURVE_SMOOTH=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AB_UNIFORM_EVEN_SELECTOR_GENUS=N(alpha)-3.
RESULT_229AB_EVERY_SURVIVING_PRIMITIVE_EVEN_SELECTOR_HAS_GENUS_GT1=PROVED_EXACT.


11. Faltings closes every fixed even slope


Retain the Faltings input already accepted in Stage37. For every fixed beta and sign branch, the fixed curve of Section10 has genus >1, hence finitely many Q-rational parameter values.


On the PLUS branch, a fixes h=-2a^2 and therefore
  q=-(h+h^{-1})/2
up to the finite reciprocal/orientation choice.


On the MINUS branch, u fixes q through the same rational conic parameter relation as229X.


In either branch
  q=d t^2
with d the canonical positive squarefree twist. Thus each surviving parameter fixes one canonical d. Consequently every fixed primitive even slope realizes only finitely many canonical twists.


Retain229L: each fixed canonical d contributes B^{o(1)} positive physical endpoints of R_phys<=B. Therefore for every fixed primitive even alpha,
  P_alpha(B)=B^{o(1)}.                            (229AB.26)


RESULT_229AB_EACH_PRIMITIVE_EVEN_SLOPE_COUNT=B^{o(1)}.


12. All bounded even dependence, and then all dependence, is negligible


Retain229S on the preferred large-radical tail:
  N(alpha)<=M_delta,
with M_delta independent of B.
Hence only finitely many primitive even alpha occur. Summing (229AB.26) over that finite set gives
  #{dependent endpoints on the preferred large-radical tail
      with N(alpha) even}
    =B^{o(1)}
    =o(B^{1/3}).                                  (229AB.27)


229AA already gives the same B^{o(1)} bound for all bounded primitive odd slopes, and229S eliminates norm2.


Therefore
  #{dependent CM-pair endpoints on the preferred large-radical tail}
    =B^{o(1)}
    =o(B^{1/3}).                                  (229AB.28)


RESULT_229AB_ALL_BOUNDED_EVEN_CM_DEPENDENCE=B^{o(1)}.
RESULT_229AB_ALL_CM_PAIR_DEPENDENCE_ON_PREFERRED_LARGE_TAIL=B^{o(1)}.
RESULT_229AB_CM_PAIR_DEPENDENCE_SUBGATE=CLOSED_FOR_STAGE37_ONE_THIRD_BUDGET.


This is a genuine subgate closure. It is NOT whole-population counting credit.


13. What remains open


The CM-pair INDEPENDENT branch remains OPEN. This card proves that dependence is negligible; it does not provide a quantitative theorem counting independent pairs.


The whole-population preferred gate remains unchanged:
  #{positive primitive physical endpoints R_phys<=B:
      sf(gcd(e R_phys, x y))>B^(1/3-delta)}
    =o(B^(1/3))
for some fixed delta>0.


GAUSSIAN_TWIST_RADICAL_GCD remains CONDITIONAL_RESERVE/THEOREM_WATCH.


NEXT_USEFUL_INPUT:

(B) direct same-physical radical-support theorem for the preferred whole-population gate;
(C) selector-conditioned/twist-support count meeting the same B^(1/3) budget.


DO_NOT_CONTINUE:

- no further odd fixed-norm iteration unless hostile audit rejects229AA;
- do not promote dependence closure to the independent CM-pair branch;

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AA — uniform primitive odd-CM selector smoothness and total odd-dependence closure


STATUS: POST_229Z_UNIFORM_ODD_CM_SELECTOR_THEOREM / PROVED_H_ALPHA_DESCENDS_TO_X_LINE / PROVED_UNIFORM_ZERO_POLE_SEPARATION_BY_GAUSSIAN_COPRIMALITY / PROVED_FIXED_SELECTOR_CURVE_SMOOTH_GENUS_N_MINUS_2_FOR_EVERY_PRIMITIVE_ODD_ALPHA / PROVED_ALL_BOUNDED_ODD_CM_DEPENDENCE_Bo1 / ODD_CM_DEPENDENCE_SUBGATE_CLOSED / GLOBAL_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229Z UNIFORM CM DIVISOR THEOREM / ODD-NORM SELECTOR CURVE CLASSIFICATION / FINITE-SLOPE CLOSURE


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229Z
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229W proved the all-odd pullback/rationalization theorem. For every primitive odd Gaussian dependence slope
  alpha=a+bi in Z[i],
with a,b nonzero coprime integers and
  n=N(alpha)=a^2+b^2 odd,
a physical dependent endpoint has
  Q in E_d(Q),
  P=[alpha]Q,
  r=X(Q)/d=epsilon*t^2,  epsilon in {+1,-1}.
For each fixed alpha the only remaining condition is the physical base selector N(p) in Q^{*2}.


Cards 229U/229W/229Y/229Z closed n=5,13,17,25 one by one by explicit fixed curves. The observed genus pattern is not accidental. This card proves a uniform divisor-theoretic theorem for every primitive odd alpha and closes ALL odd slopes in the bounded 229S dependence gate at once.


No global Stage37 gate is closed.


2. Retained odd CM square-root and descent to the X-line


Work over
  K=Q(i),
  E_d: Y^2=X^3-d^2X,
  T0=(0,0),
  O=point at infinity.


Retain 229W:
  F_alpha := (X composed [alpha])/X = H_alpha^2      (229AA.1)
for some H_alpha in K(E_d)^*.


The divisor is
  div(H_alpha)
   =[alpha]^*(T0-O)-(T0-O).                         (229AA.2)


Both T0 and O are fixed by [-1], and [alpha] commutes with [-1], so this divisor is [-1]-invariant. Normalize the 229W square root at O. Then
  H_alpha(-P)/H_alpha(P)
is a constant with value +1 at O. Therefore
  H_alpha(-P)=H_alpha(P),
so H_alpha belongs to the even subfield
  K(X) subset K(E_d).                              (229AA.3)


Thus write
  H_alpha(X)=c_alpha A_alpha(X)/B_alpha(X),
with c_alpha in K^* and coprime A_alpha,B_alpha in K[X].


RESULT_229AA_H_ALPHA_DESCENDS_TO_X_LINE=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Zero and pole structure on E_d


Multiplication by alpha is etale in characteristic zero and has degree n.


The zero divisor in (229AA.2) consists of
  [alpha]^{-1}(T0) minus {T0},
and the pole divisor consists of
  ker[alpha] minus {O}.                            (229AA.4)


Because n is odd, a and b have opposite parity. Modulo2, alpha acts on E_d[2] as either the unit 1 or the unit i. Both are bijections of E_d[2], and both fix T0. Hence:
- T0 is the only 2-torsion point mapping to T0 under [alpha];
- ker[alpha] contains no nontrivial 2-torsion.


Therefore every remaining zero and pole in (229AA.4) is non-2-torsion and occurs in a distinct pair {P,-P}. Since [alpha] is etale, every such point has multiplicity one on E_d.


It follows on the X-line that
  deg A_alpha=deg B_alpha=(n-1)/2,                (229AA.5)
and A_alpha and B_alpha are individually squarefree and coprime over K.


RESULT_229AA_FIXED_ALPHA_ZERO_POLE_SIMPLE=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AA_FIXED_ALPHA_DEGREES=(n-1)/2.


4. Gaussian coprimality separates every conjugate support


Because gcd(a,b)=1 and n is odd,
  gcd_{Z[i]}(alpha,bar(alpha))=1.                  (229AA.6)


Proof: a common Gaussian prime divides
  alpha+bar(alpha)=2a
and
  alpha-bar(alpha)=2bi.
The prime 1+i cannot divide alpha because n is odd. Any other common prime lies over an odd rational prime dividing both a and b, contradicting gcd(a,b)=1.


Hence choose u,v in Z[i] with
  u alpha+v bar(alpha)=1.                         (229AA.7)


Now compare the supports of A_alpha,B_alpha and their coefficient conjugates.


If a common X-root of A_alpha and bar(A_alpha) existed, choose P above that X-value. Since T0=-T0,
  [alpha]P=T0,
  [bar(alpha)]P=T0.
Equation (229AA.7) gives
  P=[u+v]T0 in E_d[2].
But [alpha] is bijective on E_d[2] and only T0 maps to T0, so P=T0, which is precisely the canceled point and is not a root of A_alpha. Contradiction.


If a common root of B_alpha and bar(B_alpha) existed, then
  [alpha]P=O,
  [bar(alpha)]P=O,
and (229AA.7) gives P=O, again the canceled point rather than a finite B_alpha-root.


If a common root occurred between a zero-support factor and a pole-support conjugate, for example
  [alpha]P=T0,
  [bar(alpha)]P=O,
then (229AA.7) gives P=[u]T0 in {O,T0}; neither possibility satisfies both equations. The other cross cases are identical.


Therefore all four finite support sets attached to
  A_alpha, bar(A_alpha), B_alpha, bar(B_alpha)
are pairwise disjoint except for the already canceled O/T0 points, and each is simple.


RESULT_229AA_GAUSSIAN_COPRIMALITY=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AA_CONJUGATE_ZERO_POLE_SUPPORTS_PAIRWISE_DISJOINT=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Uniform fixed-selector curve and genus formula


For rational r, coefficient conjugation gives
  N_{K/Q}(H_alpha(r))
